data.title: Side Effect
data.tagline: A function or request changes external state or triggers an external action beyond returning a value
data.learningOutcome: You can separate preview from submission, give effects an explicit trigger, and verify the resulting external state.
data.description: A price preview can calculate and return shipping without creating a quote or sending email. Saving the order and notifying the user are intentional side effects when the user explicitly submits. A side effect is not automatically an error; it needs a clear trigger and observable result.

learning.assumes: You know that a function or request can change a database, file, message, or other external state.
learning.outcome: You can separate preview from submission, give effects an explicit trigger, and verify the resulting external state.

distinctions.label: Idempotency
distinctions.explanation: Side Effect refers to state mutations on external systems; Idempotency ensures repeated requests only apply critical side effects once.

explanation.title: Problem and key mechanism
explanation.text: The user only wants a shipping and total preview, but the old endpoint writes a quote and sends email; separate preview calculation from explicit submission so Confirm order alone saves and notifies.

explanation.title: How to observe the improvement
explanation.text: Save the order, decrement stock, or send notifications only after explicit confirmation, and return the real status of each action. Verify that preview adds no record or email, while one confirmed submission creates the expected record and notification once.

explanation.title: A second scenario: content publishing
explanation.text: Previewing an article should not publish the draft or notify subscribers. Those external changes should wait for an explicit Publish action, with the publication state and notification result checked separately.

data.boundary: A side effect is not an error. Database writes, emails, and logs can be intentional; the trigger, scope, and result should be explicit and observable rather than pretending there are no effects.

lessonPractice.title: The preview endpoint adds a quote and sends email on every call. What is the best adjustment?

options.label: Make preview calculate and return the price; save and notify only on explicit submit
options.feedback: Correct. Each action has a clear trigger, so you can verify no change during preview and one order during submission.

options.label: Keep the preview write but send the email silently in the background
options.feedback: Hiding the email does not remove the effect; previews still create records and users cannot tell when order data appeared.

options.label: Check only that the preview price is correct and ignore database or email results
options.feedback: A correct price does not prove that no record or email was created; both preview and submit effects must be checked.

data.agentPrompt: Separate quote preview from order submission: preview should calculate and return the price without writing a quote or sending email; only an explicit Confirm order should save and notify once. Add tests proving preview adds no record or email and one submission creates the expected external effects once.
